chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Saif ibn 'Amirah and Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shammam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) freed one thousand slaves from the earnings of his own hand.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.مِنْ كَدِّ يَدِهِ: From the earnings of his hand (manual labor)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali free slaves using his own earnings?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on earning (*al-Makasib*), this narration underscores the virtue of manual labor (*kadd al-yad*) as a legitimate and noble source of wealth for the Imams. It illustrates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) commitment to self-sufficiency and his practical application of emancipating slaves as a means of spiritual purification and social justice, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the moral dimensions of economic activity.
